title: A held village keeps its people: each one is back 10 to 15 s after he falls, in the same job, where nobody is looking
rule: Where the Resistance holds a place and a fight goes on round it, its people do not run out: when one dies, the same person (the same job and kit: the man who hands out rockets, the medic) comes back 10 to 15 s later from a spot indoors close by, never while a player can see that spot, and his body fades. The few the story needs never die. When the fight is over the comebacks stop. Changing how the Resistance base's people die and come back: ask the owner first.
why: d2_coast_03 (New Little Odessa): citizen_b_regular_respawn, citizen_a_ammo_respawn (ammosupply RPG_Round) and citizen_a_medic_respawn each OnDeath > their own npc_template_maker Enable @10; each maker sits under the house (radius 256, maxnpccount 1, maxlivechildren 1, spawnflags 176: fade corpse, infinite children, don't spawn while visible) and Disables itself OnSpawnNPC. The gatekeeper is critical: his death ends the game (killed_critical_npc, GAMEOVER_ALLY). d2_coast_10 (the lighthouse): citizen_spawner_1 and 2 spawnfrequency 15, Killed when the gunship comes (gunship1_spawner OnSpawnNPC). Valve's wiki (vdc.py --card npc_template_maker): the don't-spawn-while-visible flag is broken in multiplayer.
how: Gamemode (ask first): a Resistance base NPC who dies is made again after about 12 s at a spot inside, picked where no player has a line of sight (our own check in Lua: the maker's flag does not work in multiplayer), with the same name and job; no comebacks once the raid is over. Map modules: a hidden spawn spot inside each base room.

title: A village's lookout sits high with a hand siren: he sounds it, the attacker kills him first, and the siren dies with a squeal
rule: A place the Resistance holds has one lookout up high (a tower or a roof, about 300 over the ground) who sits watching. When the attack comes he sounds a hand siren heard across the place (about 1250 round) that winds up over 10 s and down over 50; the attacker goes for him first; when he falls the siren stops with a squeal and the tower's loose things come down. Players learn the attack has begun from a sound and a man, not a line of text. A lookout or a siren at our base: ask the owner first.
why: d2_coast_03: citizen_tower_guy (point_template at 6996 5013 708; the village floor is about 300 to 400) sits on an info_node_hint (hinttype 12, a look-about busy scene). gunship_arrival_relay > radio_siren > ag_siren PlaySound (two ambient_generic, coast.siren_citizen and coast.bunker_siren1, radius 1250, spinup 10, spindown 50); ai_relationship gunship_vs_tower_guy_hate (rank 999999) makes him the gunship's first target; his OnDeath > radio_sirensqueal (coast.siren_squeal) and ag_siren StopSound; gunship_arrival_relay2 > tower_props EnableMotion. The siren is stopped 60 s on in any case (ag_siren StopSound @60).
how: Map modules: a lookout seat (a hint, a siren prop and its sound) on the Resistance base's roof. Gamemode (ask first): a raid on the base starts with the siren from the lookout's spot, and his death stops it.

title: An aircraft attacking a place circles it on a few loops, switching at random every 7 to 12 s, and keeps pace with players along a long way
rule: A gunship attacking a village does not hover in one spot: it flies one of three loops round the place and picks another at random every 7 to 12 s, so cover that works now does not work for long. It goes for the lookout first and turns on the player once he hurts it. Along a long way (a bridge) it keeps pace with the player: zones along the way, 450 to 1900 apart, each send it to the stretch of path beside that zone and wake only the zones next to it. When it falls: music, the siren stops, people come out and talk, a save. NPC aircraft are new to our city: ask the owner first.
why: d2_coast_03: gunship1_pathtimer (logic_timer, random 7 to 12 s) > gunship1_randompath (logic_case PickRandom) > gunship1 SetTrack path_village_a_1, b_1 or c_1; gunship1 OnFirstDamage > gunship_vs_player_hate (rank 3); citizens_vs_gunship (hate) starts active; OnDeath > gunshipdown_music @3, ag_siren StopSound, the follow goals Killed, ss_post* BeginSequence @2, autosave @7. d2_coast_08: gunship_trigger_1 to 9 along the bridge deck (y -2701 to 4544; gaps 669, 1328, 448, 1920, 448, 1152, 592, 688) each SetTrack path_a_N and Enable only their neighbours. d2_coast_10: the gunship and four dropships come from npc_template_makers.
how: Gamemode (ask first): if the owner wants a Combine aircraft over a raid, give it three loops over the place with a random switch every 7 to 12 s, turning on players who shoot it. Map modules: three path loops over the Resistance base and over the plaza.

title: A lambda on a wall marks a cache: one a map, the supplies a few steps from it
rule: Along a long road the Resistance marks its caches with the lambda: one mark a map, and 25 to 250 from it (median 60) a cache of 2 to 9 things within 400: crates to break, a medkit, batteries, grenades, mostly on the ground under the mark. Players learn that the orange lambda means help close by and look round it. Our way marks point the way to Resistance ground; a cache by a mark is new: ask the owner first.
why: infodecal or info_overlay lambdaspray in d2_coast_01, 03, 04, 05, 07, 09 and 11 (one each; none in 08, 10 or d1_trainstation_06). Nearest supply to the mark 58, 153, 24, 246, 30, 26 and 92 (median 58); within 400: item_item_crate 13, item_battery 4, item_ammo_smg1_grenade 4, item_healthkit 3, item_dynamic_resupply 2. The supply sits a median 20 below the mark.
how: Editor (ask first): a way mark could carry an optional stash beside it (a crate or a small box) that refills slowly. Map modules: a lambda and a crate together in the Resistance's back ways.

title: A Combine squad mixes its guns: about half SMG, a quarter AR2, a fifth shotgun, and is named for the place it holds
rule: Soldiers are not armed alike: across a fight about 56% carry the SMG, 25% the AR2 and 19% the shotgun, and most squads of three or more carry at least two kinds. Each squad is named for the place it holds (the dock, the crane, warehouse 1, the gas station, the ruined house) and is 2 to 8 strong; half carry 5 grenades and half never run out. Changing what our Combine NPCs carry: ask the owner first.
why: 100 npc_combine_s in d2_coast_03, 04, 05, 07, 08, 09 and 10 (all combine_soldier.mdl, skin 0): additionalequipment smg1 56, ar2 25, shotgun 19; numgrenades 5 on 51, 999999 on 48. 23 squads, 1 to 16 strong (median 3); 12 carry all three guns, 16 an AR2, 14 a shotgun. Names: dock_squad, crane_squad, warehouse1_squad, warehouse2_squad (d2_coast_04); gas_station_squad, ruined_house_gang, rockpile_gang (05); bridge_squad_1, bridgevillage_soldier_squad (07).
how: Gamemode (ask first): when the city spawns Combine NPCs for a raid or a post, deal guns in that mix within each squad.
check: a test can count the guns in a spawned squad

title: A train at a crossing: two red lamps blink in turn, a bell rings while it passes, and the train carries its own sounds and hurts whoever stands on the line
rule: Where a line crosses a way people walk, a passing train is announced: two red lamps side by side blink in turn every half second and a bell rings for as long as the train passes (25 s), then both stop; the train carries its own idle, horn and brake sounds, and a hurt brush rides with it (20 a touch) so the line is no place to stand. Blinking lamps cross the owner's rule against flickering lights, and trains belong to Civil Intake's arrivals: ask the owner first.
why: d1_trainstation_06: first_train_rl (logic_relay) > first_train_1 to 4 SetSpeed 0.7; sprite_crossing_1 ShowSprite and sprite_crossing_2 HideSprite @1; timer_crossing_lights (refire 0.5) Enable @1 > both ToggleSprite; train_bell (train_crossing_bell, radius 2174) PlaySound @1, StopSound @25; the timer Disable @25, both sprites HideSprite @26. The two env_sprite (glow01, 255 0 0, scale 1) stand 13 apart. ambient_generic train_idle, train_horn_1 and train_brake have sourceentityname first_train_1 (radius 1250); first_train_hurtbrushes (trigger_hurt, damagecap 20) is parented to the train. 54 path_track OnPass > SetSpeed lines run the yard's trains.
how: Map modules (ask first): a crossing piece by the station (two lamps, a bell, the relay), fired when Civil Intake's train comes in.

extra.how: HL2's coast (d2_coast_01, 03, 04): an env_player_surface_trigger (gamematerial 78, sand; Valve's wiki says it is meant for single player) Enables the antlion maker when the player steps on sand and Disables it 0 to 1 s after he steps off; the maker spawns round the player with two settings, on foot (pool regen 3 every 20 s, 4 alive, one every 0.2 s, radius 600) and in the car (regen 1 every 1 s, 3 alive, radius 700); point_antlion_repellant (radius 200 to 700) keep them off rocks, roads and docks; thumpers there reach 1000; d2_coast_11's sand crossing spawns 1000 round the player, 5 alive, one every 0.35 s.

The coast road's poles (utilitypole01b) stand 1022 to 1788 apart (nearest of the same model in d2_coast_01, 04, 09, 10) with spans of median 1052 to 1764 and slack 100 to 105, width 1: twice the city's span with the same sag.

d2_coast_10 (the lighthouse): four dropships from npc_template_makers bring the waves; one whose crate is shot down before it lands (OnCrateShotDownBeforeDropoff) leaves at once and is counted; 5 to 10 s after each one appears the rebels' shout conditions are enabled (they call for rockets); the rebels come back every 15 s until the gunship arrives.

The coast's Resistance posts have the same radio corner, bigger: New Little Odessa's house (d2_coast_03) has four receivers, two more on a cart, a radio, an antenna, a control desk and five storage closets, with six floodlamps outside; the lighthouse (d2_coast_10) two receivers, a radio and the canal map, which also hangs in d2_coast_01's dock post.
